chunks: I asked him about God — can He be described? So he said: 'Do you not read the Quran?' I said: 'Yes.'
He said: 'Do you not read His saying, the Exalted: "Visions cannot comprehend Him, and He comprehends (all) visions" [6:103]?' I said: 'Yes.'
He said: 'So do you recognize the visions?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'What are they?' I said: 'Visions of the eyes.'
So he said: 'Indeed, the imaginations of the hearts are greater than the visions of the eyes. So He is such that the imaginations cannot comprehend Him, and He comprehends the imaginations.'

key_terms.الأبصار: Visions/sights — the faculty of physical eyesight; here extended metaphorically
key_terms.الأوهام: Imaginations/conceptions — the heart's capacity to form mental images or concepts
key_terms.يدرك: To comprehend, perceive, or grasp fully — a technical theological term indicating total perception

ai.seo_question: Can God be described or comprehended according to Imam al-Reza?
ai.summary: Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari reports asking Imam al-Reza (peace be upon him) whether God can be described. The Imam responded by invoking the Quranic verse 6:103 — which declares that physical sight cannot comprehend God — and then extended this argument: if the eye's vision fails, so does the heart's imagination, which is an even more expansive faculty. This hadith establishes a key principle in Shia rational theology (kalam): God is beyond all human perception, whether physical or mental, and any attempt to circumscribe Him within human categories is inherently inadequate.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abu Hashim Al Ja’fary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, can He<sup>azwj</sup> be described?’
So heasws said: ‘Did you not read the Words of the Exalted [6:103] Visions cannot comprehend Him, and He Comprehends (all) visions?’ I said, ‘Yes’.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So are you recognising the ‘visions’?’ I said, ‘Yes’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What are these?’ I said, ‘Visions of the eyes’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The imaginations of the hearts are greater than the visions of the eyes. So He<sup>azwj</sup> is such that the imaginations cannot comprehend Him<sup>azwj</sup> and He<sup>azwj</sup> Comprehends the imaginations (of the creatures)’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abu Hashim al-Ja‘fari who has said the following. “I asked Imam abul Hassan al-Rida (a.s.), about Allah if He can be described (defined in words). The Imam (a.s.) said, “Have you not read the Quran?” I replied, “Yes, I do read the Quran.”
He then said, “Have you not read the words of Allah, the Most High, “No mortal eyes can see Him, but He can see all eyes. He is All-kind and All-aware.” [6:103] I replied, “Yes, I have read them.”
The Imam (a.s.) said, “Do they know the meaning of the eyes?” I replied, “Yes, they do.” The Imam (a.s.) said, “What is it?” I replied, “ It means seeing with the eyes.”
Then the Imam said, the Awham (mentioned above) of the heart is far greater comprehensive in knowledge than eye-witnessing. It is not able to comprehend Him but He comprehends all things.”
